info.name: ENVISION Design API
info.description: ENVISION Design API collection aligned with Controllers/DesignController.cs (routes under /API/Design). Use this to create or update graphical design objects via REST when content is too large to pass through MCP — most importantly ImageObject images, where the base64 data URL goes in attributes.data-imgsrc of the request body. IMPORTANT: the collection variables base_url, username and password are DUMMY PLACEHOLDERS. Replace them with the real ENVISION server URL and an Administrators-group user before sending any request. All requests use collection-level HTTP Basic auth. Create uses POST /API/Design/Objects with a body containing pageName and an objects array; do NOT include attributes.id on create. Update uses PUT /API/Design/Objects with attributes.id identifying each object. An update is PARTIAL: include only the attributes you want to change - attributes.type and attributes.data-objectname are NOT required (an attribute the update does not mention keeps its stored value, so there is no need to read the object and resend its name), and omitting data-imgsrc preserves the existing image. Required attributes are enforced on create only. A PUT batch is applied as ONE page save like a create batch: nothing is written unless every item validates, and the error names the item with itemIndex and itemPath. A GroupObject item may carry a children array on update too - a child with attributes.id is updated, a child without one is CREATED inside that group - so growing a group box and adding a part to it happen in the same call. For ImageObject the server auto-sizes the object to the image's pixel dimensions on create. Note on size: the whole request body must stay under the server's 30,000,000-byte (about 28.6 MB) limit, so after base64 expansion the largest practical image file is roughly 22 MB; larger images return HTTP 413. Tip: build the base64 from the file with tooling (e.g. the base64 command) and inject it into the body; do not type it by hand. Field names are strict on the UDT symbol, map children, bind and delete endpoints: a field the endpoint does not define is refused with HTTP 400 naming it, instead of being ignored. Object position and size are attributes (top, left, width, height, z-index), never fields of the request body itself. Shape geometry: for PolygonObject/PolylineObject the object's width and height are derived from the bounding box of data-points, so omit width/height when sending data-points (contradicting values are rejected with a validation error). data-points accepts x/y pairs separated by any mix of spaces and commas (both '0 50,50 100,100 50' and '0,75 50,0 100,75' styles work for both types); malformed lists and too few points (3 minimum for polygon, 2 for polyline) are rejected instead of silently keeping the default template shape. Points not starting at 0 are normalized and the difference is applied to left/top; a child of a GroupObject is rejected if this (or an explicit negative left/top) would make its offset negative, because the API does not recalculate the group's box. Bare numbers for data-fontsize, data-borderradius and border widths are treated as px. Batch rule: a create batch is applied as ONE page save, so a batch that fails validation anywhere creates nothing and can simply be corrected and resent; the error names the offending item with itemIndex (its index in the objects array) and itemPath (its full path, e.g. objects[4].children[1]). A GroupObject's children are created in the SAME call by nesting them in a children array on the item, not by a second call carrying parentId: the parent's id is generated by that create, so the caller cannot know it beforehand. parentId stays available for adding objects to a group that already exists, and is refused on a nested child, which already has its parent. Group box rule: omit width/height when creating a GroupObject and the API derives the box from the children's extent; a supplied box is kept as-is but children must fit inside it — a create or geometry update that leaves a child reaching outside the group box is rejected with the required size in the error, because the API does not re-normalize group geometry the way the designer does.

request.description: Create one or more design objects. For an ImageObject, put the full base64 data URL in attributes.data-imgsrc. Do NOT include attributes.id on create (the server generates it). The server auto-sizes the ImageObject to the image's pixel dimensions. Replace <BASE64> with the base64 of your image file (e.g. produced by the base64 command).

Update one or more existing design objects. attributes.id is required and identifies the object. attributes.type and attributes.data-objectname are also required on every update (resend the object's current data-objectname, available from the GET response) even when you only intend to change one other attribute. Include only the additional attributes you want to change. For an ImageObject, set attributes.data-imgsrc to a new base64 data URL to replace the image; omit data-imgsrc to keep the existing image.

Create a MapObject. Do NOT include attributes.id on create (the server generates it). data-map-style selects the basemap preset and accepts street, terrain, light, dark, humanitarian or satellite. data-map-lockview set to true prevents the runtime user from panning or zooming. data-map-center is "lat,lon" in decimal degrees. data-map-zoom is an integer zoom level; the runtime clamps it to the maximum zoom of the selected style (terrain 17, light and dark 20, the others 19). Only the map container is managed through this API. The symbols placed on the map are group symbol instances maintained from the designer through Edit Map Children.

Update an existing MapObject. attributes.id is required and identifies the object. attributes.type and attributes.data-objectname are also required on every update (resend the object's current data-objectname, available from the GET response) even when you only intend to change one other attribute. Include only the additional attributes you want to change. Changing data-map-style can lower the effective maximum zoom, in which case the runtime clamps data-map-zoom. Map children are group symbol instances and are not updated through this request.

Create one or more Document Viewer objects. The object shows a document inline on a runtime page over an authenticated URL, so the file never has to be published anonymously. data-documentpath is the FULL path of the file, or the name of a variable holding one. What may be served is decided entirely by the DocumentViewerAccess parameter: the file's folder must be listed there or be below a listed folder, the caller must be logged in, and Guests are always refused. An empty matrix serves nothing at all. Served types: pdf, png, jpg, jpeg, gif, txt. data-statusvariable is optional and names a client.* variable the object publishes its state to (ok, nopath, unavailable, signin), so a page can say why the frame is empty instead of showing a blank area. Do NOT include attributes.id on create (the server generates it).

Update one or more existing Document Viewer objects. attributes.id is required and identifies the object. attributes.type and attributes.data-objectname are also required on every update (resend the object's current data-objectname, available from the GET response) even when you only intend to change one other attribute. This example binds the path to a client variable, so an operator decides which document the frame shows.

item.name: Create Design Objects (POST) - DropDownObject from a document folder

request.description: Create a DropDown that lists the documents that ACTUALLY EXIST in a folder, instead of items configured by hand. Set data-documentfolder (a folder, or the name of a variable holding one) and the object stops using data-items/data-values: it reads the folder each time the operator opens the list, shows the label chosen by data-documentlabel (name, date or datetime) and writes the FULL PATH of the picked document to data-variable. Point a DocumentViewerObject's data-documentpath at that same variable and the operator has a working report picker without any page having to construct a file name. data-documentpattern filters by file name AND is the only place a document's date can come from. * and ? are wildcards; adding strftime date tokens declares where the date sits and how it is written, so Report_%d-%m-%Y.pdf and Report_%m-%d-%Y.pdf read the very same files differently and neither is a guess. Tokens: %Y year, %y two-digit year, %m month, %d day, %H hour, %M minute, %S second - fixed width, zero-padded, case-sensitive (%m month versus %M minute), with %% for a literal percent. Because every token starts with %, all other text is literal as typed and needs no quoting. Nothing is inferred from a file name: without a complete date the document has no date, from/to are ignored, and the Date label shows the file name. data-documentfrom/data-documentto are inclusive and compare to the precision the pattern declared, so Report_%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S.pdf supports a window such as 08:00 to 11:00; a bound with no time part covers the whole day. Bind them to client variables written by two ordinary DateTimePickers, or point BOTH at the same variable so one picker means one single day. An empty or unreadable bound is no bound, so a page whose date variable has not arrived yet shows the whole folder rather than an empty list. Access is the Document Viewer's: the folder must be listed in the DocumentViewerAccess parameter for one of the caller's user groups, the listing is not recursive, and only file types the viewer serves are returned. data-statusvariable is optional and names a client.* variable receiving ok, empty, unavailable or signin. The same attributes work on a ListBoxObject. Do NOT include attributes.id on create (the server generates it).

Create one or more viewer objects. AlarmViewerObject, EventViewerObject, AuditTrailViewerObject, TrendAnalystViewerObject and UsersViewerObject each frame one fixed in-product page. They carry NO address: the runtime resolves the route itself, relative to whatever host, IP or port the client used, so a remote client needs no configuration. The framed page keeps enforcing its own user-group rights. Only TrendAnalystViewerObject has a setting of its own: data-config holds a Trend Analyst configuration as JSON, or the name of a variable holding it (a client variable in the example below), which is pushed into the frame and applied live. Do NOT include attributes.id on create (the server generates it).

Update one or more existing viewer objects. attributes.id is required and identifies the object. attributes.type and attributes.data-objectname are also required on every update (resend the object's current data-objectname, available from the GET response) even when you only intend to change one other attribute. This example replaces the bound variable with a literal Trend Analyst configuration.

item.name: Create Design Objects (POST) - GroupObject with children

request.description: Create a group and everything inside it in ONE call by nesting the children in a children array on the item. This is the only way to create a group's children together with the group: a child cannot name its parent through parentId, because the parent's id is generated by this very call. children is accepted on GroupObject only, may nest further (a group inside a group), and a nested child that also carries parentId is refused. Because the whole batch is one page save, a failure anywhere creates nothing, and the group's box is derived from ALL of its children: this example omits the group's width/height and the server stores 160x120, the extent of the circle and the label. The response lists objectIds in creation order - the group first, then its children depth-first. Use parentId instead when adding an object to a group that already exists on the page. Do NOT include attributes.id on create.

item.name: Create Design Objects (POST) - PolylineObject with arrowheads and bridges

request.description: PolylineObject with flow arrowheads and crossing bridges. data-arrowstart / data-arrowend accept None, Arrow (filled triangle) or OpenArrow; data-arrowsize is the head length as a multiple of data-strokewidth (default 4, minimum 6 pixels). data-bridge set to 'true' makes this line hop over the other polylines it crosses, as used on piping and electrical diagrams; data-bridgesize is the hop radius as a multiple of data-strokewidth (default 2.5, minimum 4 pixels). Crossings are detected from live page geometry, so no coordinates are stored and moving either line updates the hops. A line only hops over the lines it is drawn ON TOP OF, so give it a higher z-index than the lines it should hop over. The arc bulges to the left of the direction the points run in. Width and height are derived from data-points, so do not send them.

Continuous rotation. data-rotateenable turns a free-running spin on and accepts 'true'/'false', a variable or an expression, so a symbol can turn only while its run feedback is on. data-rotatespeed is DEGREES PER SECOND (larger is faster, default 90, a negative value reverses) and also accepts a variable or expression, so the symbol can follow a measured speed. data-rotatedirection is Clockwise (default) or CounterClockwise. It composes with the fixed data-transformrotate angle rather than replacing it. Applied on SVGObject, ImageObject, LabelObject, SquareObject, CircleObject and PolygonObject. Continuous rotation runs in runtime only; the design canvas keeps the object still so it stays selectable.

Get a structure and identity summary of all design objects on a page. Each object carries only id, type, top, left, width, height, z-index, parentId, data-objectname, data-groupsymbol, data-groupsymbolmaster, data-udtinstance and data-mapchild; all other data-* attributes are omitted so large pages stay within client response limits. An attribute missing from this listing is not absent from the object - fetch the full attribute set with Get Object Details, which accepts multiple objectIds per call.

Get one or more design objects by id with all their data-* attributes. Repeat the objectIds query parameter for each id (objectIds=A&objectIds=B). This is the detail read: use it to inspect an object's configuration or verify writes, since the Get Objects listing is a summary that omits most attributes. The response returns the requested objects in objects and lists any id that did not resolve in notFound; an unresolved id never fails the batch. Request modest batches, since every object carries its full attribute set. For PolygonObject and PolylineObject the response also returns data-points, in the canonical form written on save, so a routed line can be read back and edited instead of re-authored; the summary listing still omits it. A group child is an ordinary object here: take its id from the listing (its parentId is the group) and read its geometry the same way.
Delete one or more design objects by id.

Position and size belong in attributes, as the plain keys top, left, width, height and z-index (a bare number is read as px). The symbol is a clone of its master, so leaving top/left out places it at the master's own coordinates. Unknown fields at the root of the body are rejected with 400. The response reports the stored left/top.
